_comment: Example board-language sidecar for the posture section, the shape the ciso-board-translation skill produces. Pass to render_executive.py with --translations. Every figure here is read from examples/example-profile.csfp — 21 Subcategories in scope, 9 assessed, 6 carrying a gap — the skill supplies structure and judgment, never invented numbers. Keys are optional: omit any and that slot renders as a labelled placeholder. The canonical item key is "gaps"; "subcategories" is a deprecated alias kept readable for older sidecars. See skills/board-pack/references/section-contract.md.
executiveSummary: Twenty-one outcomes are in scope this cycle and nine of them have been assessed, so this is a partial picture and should be read as one. Of what we have looked at, six fall short of the target we set. The distance is not evenly spread. Two sit at Not Achieved against a target we chose deliberately, which means the work has not started rather than that it is going slowly: encryption of data at rest, and supply-chain risk management. A third — our risk-assessment outcome — carries a full-size gap for a different reason, that we have not assessed it yet, and it would be wrong to read that as a finding. The remaining three are one step short and are the most likely to close inside the next cycle. We are asking for one decision today: fund the encryption programme, or record that the board accepts data-at-rest exposure for another two quarters.

gaps.PR.DS-01: Data at rest and in transit is at Not Achieved against a target of Fully Achieved — the widest gap in the scope, and the one most likely to be asked about first after an incident, because it decides whether a stolen disk is an inconvenience or a notification.
gaps.GV.SC-01: There is no supply-chain risk management programme, and that governs what every other control here is worth: a standard we hold ourselves to and do not hold a vendor to is a standard with a gap in it.
gaps.ID.RA-01: This outcome has not been assessed yet, so it shows the full distance to target. That is a gap in what we know, not a finding about the control — assessing it is the work, and it should not be read alongside the two outcomes we did assess and found absent.
gaps.GV.RM-01: Risk management objectives are written but not yet agreed with the leadership who own the trade-offs, so the register records our judgement rather than the organisation's.
gaps.PR.AA-01: Identity and credential management is one step short of target: the practice is in place but not applied consistently across services and hardware, which leaves the exceptions as the attack path.
gaps.GV.OC-01: Organisational mission is understood and already informs risk decisions. This is the closest to target and needs consolidation rather than investment.

decisions: Fund the data-at-rest encryption programme to close PR.DS-01, or record the board's acceptance of that exposure for a further two quarters.
Name an owner for supply-chain risk management (GV.SC-01) — the outcome cannot start without one.
Approve the assessment work to close ID.RA-01, so the next review reports a finding rather than a blank.
